instructions: 1. Pour the two example rows into your own settings list (see pour), or make list:settings from them. Keep the row for this tool under the record id record:setting:check-every-claim-against-its-facts-and-sources~film~sample-film; its settings JSON holds rules, subject_name, narrator_name and hedge_row.

2. Have the files ready: shots/<id>.json and claims/<id>.json in a lane folder, your world rows (lists.json, rows/<list>.json, relations.json), a sources file with plain-text extracts (tool:make-plain-text-extracts-of-claim-sources makes them from the raw files), and the words of your no-hedge row.

3. Write the request file {shots, lane_dir, sources, frames_root, world_dir, hedge_phrases, settings_record}. Say "Check these claims." The AI reads the row with tools:list {tool}, then runs: node tools/settings/do-work/run-with-settings.mjs --folder check-every-claim-against-its-facts-and-sources -- python3 -I tools/check-every-claim-against-its-facts-and-sources/do-work/check_claims.py < request.json

4. Read the last line {"result": {ok, shots: [{id, ok, fails, notes, lines}], world}}: exit 0 when every shot passes, 1 when one fails. Fix each failing claim by cutting it or giving it real support; never add a hedge or an attribution. An {"error"} line (exit 2) says what to change.

worked_examples.title: One plain claim passes; an unsupported claim and a hedged claim fail
worked_examples.ask: Check every claim in my three shots against my facts and sources.
worked_examples.given: Run locally from the Workshop checkout after tools:list, with the request {"shots": ["own-claim-plain", "unsupported", "attributed-hedge"], "lane_dir": "film/lane", "sources": "film/gate/sources.json", "frames_root": "film", "world_dir": "film/world", "hedge_phrases": ["she reports", "reports:", "her estimate", "estimate", "not yet tested", "reportedly"], "settings_record": {"id": "record:setting:check-every-claim-against-its-facts-and-sources~film~sample-film", "type": "record:setting", "value": "the row claim-rules-of-sample-film above, as records:read gives it"}} on stdin of check_claims.py. The folders hold the made-up world of tools/check-every-claim-against-its-facts-and-sources/test/fixture_world.py (Mara cooks cheap meals, Pip narrates): shot own-claim-plain says her mission plainly and cites fact f-mission-claim; unsupported says "Lentil soup beats every other meal." with no support; attributed-hedge says "Mara reports: the cheapest balanced meals in town, by her estimate." Observed by running do-work/check_claims.py on that fixture (settings given in the request, so no door read).
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result": {"ok": false, "shots": [{"id": "own-claim-plain", "ok": true, "fails": [], "notes": [], "lines": ["fact gate own-claim-plain: PASS"]}, {"id": "unsupported", "ok": false, "fails": ["unsupported voice 1: \"Lentil soup beats every other meal.\": cites no world fact and no source", "unsupported voice 1: \"Lentil soup beats every other meal.\": says \"every\" (scope level 3) without naming, in `strength`, the cited support that says it as strongly"], "notes": ["unsupported voice 1: names \"lentil soup\" (lentil-soup) as a reference, not a topic; declare it in `topics` if the line says something about it"]}, {"id": "attributed-hedge", "ok": false, "fails": ["attributed-hedge voice 1: \"Mara reports: the cheapest balanced meals in town, by her estimate.\": carries the hedge or attribution \"reports:\" (check row no-hedge-or-attribution): state it plainly, or cut the line if it is too weak to state plainly", "... the same line carries \"her estimate\" and \"estimate\", each reported the same way"], "notes": []}], "world": {"ok": true, "lines": ["   8  entities", "   8  facts", "   1  relations", "   5  entity kinds", "   2  fact kinds", "   1  relation roles", "   1  quotes checked against transcripts", "   7  quotes checked against file lines", "verify: ok"]}}} (exit 1; each shot's lines hold the same text with FAIL or ok prefixes)

pour.how: Name the settings list you already keep and its fields. The tool matches each kit field to one of yours (by the map you give, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), refuses when fewer than 80% match, and otherwise answers the records:write that adds the two example rows, leaving your own rows untouched.
